newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian eyes turned west for share guidance.
newsitem.headline: Belgian eyes turned west for share guidance.

text.p: Belgian shares on Thursday continued to pin their hopes on Wall Street for guidance in the absence of any domestic factors, dealers said.
At 0840 GMT, the Bel-20 index was up 0.43 percent, or 9.22 points, at 2,142.82 with about half a billion francs worth of Belgian shares traded.
Dealers said they expected the Bel-20 to pare its gains in the run-up to Wall Street's opening.
"It's waiting for the U.S. again," one trader said.
Oil firm Petrofina, which had risen more than six percent in the past two sessions, was steady at 12,775 francs.
Petrofina had been driven up mainly by warrant-related buying. The warrants give holders the right at the end of May to subscribe for an ex-dividend Petrofina share at 12,500 francs.
Other factors which had boosted the stock were the dollar and a major oil find in Angola by rival Elf-Aquitaine, dealers said. Petrofina also has interests in Angola.

Retailer Delhaize was the main gainer with a 2.0 percent rise to 1,780 but one dealer said it remained fragile in the short term as it had not yet fully digested recent weakness of its U.S. unit Food Lion.
Generale Bank issued a buy recommendation for holding firm Cobepa, which was up 0.9 percent at 1,302.
